content_units: -   Revenue trend:   up from   $4,820   in 2026-01 to   $6,710   in 2026-06
-   Total revenue change:     +$1,890   over the period
-   Strongest volume growth:     coffee   rose from   510   to   760   units
-   Likely growth driver:     coffee  , supported by steady gains in cookies and cakes
Use these 3 charts for the clearest business readout:
Chart Type   Best For   Why It’s Useful   Key Data to Plot
Line chart   Monthly trend tracking   Shows how revenue and product volumes change over time   Month on x-axis; revenue or units on y-axis
Stacked column chart   Product mix by month   Reveals how cakes, cookies, and coffee contribute to total unit sales each month   Month by stacked units for cakes, cookies, coffee
Scatter plot   Relationship to revenue   Helps show which product line most closely rises with revenue   Product units vs revenue, one series per product
A   line chart   is the best first view. Revenue increases every month, and product volumes also trend upward overall.
Chart title:   Bakery Revenue and Sales Trend
A   stacked column chart   shows that coffee is the largest product line in units every month, while cookies are the second-largest and also growing strongly.
A   scatter plot   can show which product line tracks most closely with revenue. Based on this dataset, coffee appears most strongly aligned with revenue growth because:
- it has the highest unit volume each month
- it posts the largest absolute increase:   +250 units
- its month-to-month rise is consistent alongside revenue expansion
-   Revenue is growing steadily.   There are no down months; revenue rises each month from January through June.
-   Coffee appears to be the main growth engine.   It is the highest-volume category throughout the dataset and shows the largest absolute gain.
-   Cookies are also a meaningful contributor.   Cookies increase from   340   to   490  , a gain of   150 units  , suggesting strong secondary support for growth.
-   Cakes are growing, but more modestly.   Cakes move from   120   to   172  , with a small dip in March before resuming growth.
-   Momentum strengthens after March.   From April onward, all categories climb together, which likely supports the faster revenue increases in the later months.
-   Growth is broad-based, but not evenly distributed.   All three lines improve, yet coffee’s scale makes it the most likely driver of top-line performance.
Coffee seems to be driving growth most clearly.
- Largest unit base in every month
- Revenue rises in parallel with coffee’s strong upward trend
- If management wants to double down on what’s working, coffee is the strongest candidate for promotion, bundling, and upsell strategy

This summary assumes `revenue usd` is total monthly bakery revenue and that no product-level pricing or margin data is available, so the growth driver is inferred from sales volume patterns rather than exact revenue attribution.
